q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS)/COUNT(NAME),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID=E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID ORDER BY PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS)/COUNT(NAME),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID=E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID ORDER BY PROJECT_ID
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both compute the average experience years per project by joining the PROJECT and EMPLOYEE tables and grouping by PROJECT_ID. Q1 uses AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS) while Q2 uses SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS)/COUNT(NAME). Since both approaches compute the same average (sum divided by count), the results are the same.
